prompt: Act as an Ancient Greek philologist writing learner-facing contextual glosses. These blocks are the opening of Book 1 of Marcus Aurelius' Meditations: an elliptical first-person list of qualities and practices learned from his grandfather, father, mother, and great-grandfather; a block beginning ἔτι δὲ continues the preceding lesson from his mother. The repeated governing idea [I learned] is omitted. The input columns are ID, FORM, LEMMA, coarse POS, XPOS, FEATS, HEAD, DEPREL, DEPS, MISC. Return exactly one tab-separated line for each real source-token row, in input order: its unchanged ID, a tab, then one concise English gloss. A real token has MISC beginning t_. Omit every artificial row whose MISC begins e_, even when FORM is [0], [1], or [2]; IDs may skip numbers and must never be renumbered. Select the contextual sense and express material morphology when English requires it. Keep each overt token's contribution on that token: do not move a preposition's meaning onto its noun, move a noun's meaning onto a neighboring preposition, or duplicate a relation. Translate an overt article as the, not as a supplied possessive; reserve brackets for genuinely elided arguments of content words. Render a substantivized adjective as the contextual English quality noun, not an adjective plus [quality] or [disposition]. A genitive governed by an overt preposition does not need an extra of-, and an aorist infinitive in a timeless lesson is a plain English infinitive, not a perfect infinitive. In not-only ... but-also constructions, distinguish emphatic even from merely also when context warrants it. Use hyphens instead of spaces inside one gloss. Lowercase ordinary glosses, preserve proper-name capitalization, and gloss punctuation with itself. Never copy a non-punctuation Greek FORM. Return no artificial rows, CoNLL-U rows, JSON, Markdown, blank lines, or explanation, and never put a tab or newline inside a gloss.
